# Setup

## Packages

```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library("tidyverse"))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library("lme4"))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library("Hmisc"))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library("corrplot"))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library("emmeans"))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library("performance"))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library("MASS"))
```

## Filtered data import

```{r}
data250pisum_04 <- read.csv("../../01_phenotipic_analysis/acyrthosiphon_pisum_filtered.csv", stringsAsFactors = F)
data250pisum_04$genotype <- as.factor(data250pisum_04$genotype)
```

## Data distribution

```{r}
data250pisum_04 %>% 
  ggplot(., aes(x = larvae_total_number)) + 
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5, fill = "white", color = "black") 
```

# Linear model fitting and emmeans extraction

[Useful lesson on LMMs](https://r.qcbs.ca/workshop07/book-en/fixed-vs.-random-effects.html).

## Fit linear models

```{r}
model0 <- lm(larvae_total_number ~ 1, data = data250pisum_04)
model1 <- lm(larvae_total_number ~ genotype, data = data250pisum_04)
model2 <- lmer(larvae_total_number ~ genotype + (1 | session), data = data250pisum_04)
```

```{r}
compare_performance(model0, model1, model2, rank = FALSE, verbose = TRUE)
```

::: callout-important
Model2 that models session as a random fixed factor is a slightly but significant better model.
:::

## Diagnostics

```{r}
check_model(model2)
```

::: callout-important
Most assumptions seem to be valid: normality of residuals, normality of random effects, linear relationship, homogeneity of variance, multicollinearity.
:::

## Model performances

```{r}
plot(compare_performance(model0, model1, model2))
```

```{r}
test_lrt(model0, model1)
```

```{r}
test_lrt(model1, model2)
```

# Generalized model fitting (negative binomial distribution)

```{r}
model3 <- glm.nb(formula = larvae_total_number ~ genotype, data = data250pisum_04)
#model4 <- glmer(formula = larvae_total_number ~ genotype + (genotype | session), data = data250pisum_04, family = 'poisson')
#model4 <- lme4::glmer.nb(larvae_total_number ~ genotype + (1 | session), data = data250pisum_04)
```

```{r}

model <- lmer(larvae_total_number~genotype + (1|session), data= data250pisum_04)

anova(model)

#variance stability





# Extract fitted values and residuals
fitted_values <- fitted(model)
residuals_values <- residuals(model)

#homosedasticity
# Plot residuals vs fitted values
plot(fitted_values, residuals_values, 
     main="Residuals vs Fitted", 
     xlab="Fitted values", 
     ylab="Residuals")
abline(h=0, col="red")

#residual normality
hist(residuals_values, main="Histogram of Residuals", xlab="Residuals", breaks=20)
# 2. Q-Q Plot for Residuals
qqnorm(residuals_values)
qqline(residuals_values, col = "red")

#residual independance
# Plot residuals over time (for time-series data)
plot(residuals(model), type="o", col="blue", main="Residuals over Time", xlab="Index", ylab="Residuals")


# Extract EMMeans for genotype
emm_genotype <- emmeans(model, ~ genotype)
emm_df <- as.data.frame(emm_genotype)
hist(emm_df$emmean)

# Define the file path
file_path <- "~/Documents/gitrepo/faba_specifics/01.data/emmeans_pisum.csv"

# Save the data frame to the specified location
  write.csv(emm_df, file = file_path, row.names = FALSE)


```
